packet.headline_seed: Trump says he is cancelling strikes on Iran subject to deal being made 'rapidly'
packet.description_seed: The US president claims Iran and other Middle Eastern countries asked Washington to hold off on any attack as the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed.

what: Trump says he is cancelling strikes on Iran subject to deal being made 'rapidly'

clean_source_blocks.text: Donald Trump says he has cancelled strikes against Iran provided a deal was struck "rapidly" with the country. In a post on Truth Social, the US president claimed he was asked by Iran and other countries in the Middle East to "hold off" on any attack as the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed, which he said would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending Iran's nuclear threat. His comments came after US media reported that Washington may have been planning new, intense strikes on Iran over the weekend. Earlier on Saturday, Tehran had accused the US of escalating tensions, saying any regional state co-operating with Washington would be "engulfed by the flames of war".
The US president claims Iran and other Middle Eastern countries asked Washington to hold off on any attack as the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed.

Trump further said in his post the US was "locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran, at levels of Military Terror, Strength, and Power not seen since World War II". He said cancelling the attack would be "for the future benefit of the world and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran". Iran has not yet responded to Trump's announcement. During the Friday meeting, CBS News reported Trump was heard saying while reporters were still in the room: "We'll be hitting them [Iranians] very hard. At some point, they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore.'" Axios reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke to Trump on Saturday and "expressed concern" about the potential strikes. Reuters also reported the phone call.

Washington and Tehran have engaged in escalating strikes and counter-strikes since a ceasefire in April aimed at pausing the war fell apart in June. Earlier this week, the US said it completed a "heavy wave" of strikes against Iran in retaliation for an attempted ballistic missile attack on American forces in the region. T

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World | URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cjwx74qgld2o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss]
Donald Trump says he has cancelled strikes against Iran provided a deal was struck "rapidly" with the country.

In a post on Truth Social, the US president claimed he was asked by Iran and other countries in the Middle East to "hold off" on any attack as the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed, which he said would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending Iran's nuclear threat.

His comments came after US media reported that Washington may have been planning new, intense strikes on Iran over the weekend.

Earlier on Saturday, Tehran had accused the US of escalating tensions, saying any regional state co-operating with Washington would be "engulfed by the flames of war".

Meanwhile the US government urged Americans across the Middle East to be alert and ready to leave "should there be escalation" in the region.

"Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise caution and heightened vigilance and should be prepared for flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions," the security alert said on Saturday.

Multiple sources had earlier told CBS News, the BBC's American media partner, that the US and Israel were planning what would be one of the harshest bombing campaigns to date against energy infrastructure targets in Iran.

The plan came up during Trump's cabinet meeting on Friday, sources told CBS News.

Trump further said in his post the US was "locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran, at levels of Military Terror, Strength, and Power not seen since World War II".

He said cancelling the attack would be "for the future benefit of the world and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran".

Iran has not yet responded to Trump's announcement.

During the Friday meeting, CBS News reported Trump was heard saying while reporters were still in the room: "We'll be hitting them [Iranians] very hard. At some point, they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore.'"

Axios reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke to Trump on Saturday and "expressed concern" about the potential strikes. Reuters also reported the phone call.

Washington and Tehran have engaged in escalating strikes and counter-strikes since a ceasefire in April aimed at pausing the war fell apart in June.

Earlier this week, the US said it completed a "heavy wave" of strikes against Iran in retaliation for an attempted ballistic missile attack on American forces in the region.

T

payload.title: Trump sanoo peruuttaneensa iskut Iraniin nopean sopimuksen ehdolla
payload.summary: Donald Trumpin mukaan Yhdysvallat pidättäytyy iskuista Iraniin, jos sopimus saadaan aikaan nopeasti. Iran ei ole vielä vastannut ilmoitukseen.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump sanoo peruuttaneensa iskut Iraniin sillä ehdolla, että sopimus syntyy nopeasti. Trumpin mukaan Iran ja muut Lähi-idän maat pyysivät Washingtonia pidättäytymään hyökkäyksestä, koska sopimuksen pääpiirteistä olisi jo sovittu.

Trump esitti ehtoja sopimukselle

Trump kirjoitti Truth Socialissa, että sopimuksen pääpiirteistä olisi sovittu. Hänen mukaansa kokonaisuuteen kuuluisivat Hormuzinsalmen avaaminen uudelleen ja Iranin aiheuttamaksi kuvaamansa ydinuhan poistaminen. Trump ei esittänyt tarkempia ehtoja eikä muuta aikataulua kuin vaatimuksen nopeasta etenemisestä. Yhdysvaltalaismediat olivat aiemmin kertoneet, että Washington saattoi suunnitella viikonlopulle uusia voimakkaita iskuja Iraniin. Trump käytti julkaisussaan samalla jyrkkää kieltä ja väitti Yhdysvaltojen olevan valmis käyttämään Irania vastaan sotilaallista voimaa, jollaista ei hänen mukaansa ole nähty sitten toisen maailmansodan. Hän perusteli iskujen peruuttamista maailman tulevalla hyödyllä sekä sillä, että Iran voisi säilyä menestyksekkäänä ja vauraana. Kyse oli Trumpin omasta arviosta, eikä Iran ole toistaiseksi vastannut hänen ilmoitukseensa. CBS Newsin mukaan Trump sanoi jo perjantaisessa tapaamisessa toimittajien vielä ollessa paikalla, että Iraniin iskettäisiin erittäin kovaa, kunnes maa ilmoittaisi, ettei se enää kestä.

Iran oli varoittanut sodan laajenemisesta

Iran oli ennen Trumpin ilmoitusta syyttänyt Yhdysvaltoja jännitteiden kiristämisestä. Se varoitti lauantaina, että Washingtonin kanssa yhteistyötä tekevät alueen valtiot joutuisivat ”sodan liekkien” keskelle. Axiosin mukaan Saudi-Arabian kruununprinssi Mohammed bin Salman keskusteli Trumpin kanssa lauantaina ja ilmaisi huolensa mahdollisista iskuista. Reuters kertoi myös puhelusta.

Iskut ja vastaiskut ovat jatkuneet

Washington ja Teheran ovat tehneet iskuja ja vastaiskuja sen jälkeen, kun sodan keskeyttämiseen tähdännyt huhtikuun tulitauko hajosi kesäkuussa. Yhdysvallat kertoi aiemmin tällä viikolla toteuttaneensa Iraniin raskaan iskujen aallon. Washingtonin mukaan kyse oli vastauksesta yritykseen iskeä ballistisella ohjuksella alueella olevia yhdysvaltalaisjoukkoja vastaan. Mahdollisten uusien iskujen toteutuminen jäi Trumpin ilmoituksessa hänen asettamansa ehdon varaan: hyökkäyksestä pidättäytyminen edellyttää hänen mukaansa sopimuksen syntymistä nopeasti.

Hänen mukaansa sopimukseen kuuluisivat Hormuzinsalmen avaaminen ja Iranin ydinuhan poistaminen.
Iran ei ole vastannut ilmoitukseen, mutta se oli aiemmin varoittanut alueellisen sodan laajenemisesta.

He said cancelling the attack would be "for the future benefit of the world and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran". Iran has not yet responded to Trump's announcement. During the Friday meeting, CBS News reported Trump was heard saying while reporters were still in the room: "We'll be hitting them [Iranians] very hard. At some point, they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore.'" Axios reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke to Trump on Saturday and "expressed concern" about the potential strikes. Reuters also reported the phone call.

Washington and Tehran have engaged in escalating strikes and counter-strikes since a ceasefire in April aimed at pausing the war fell apart in June.
